original.reason: The induction does not establish that all prime divisors of the newly constructed k_{n+1} are 3 or 1 modulo 3, although this is required for the next induction step. The asserted solvability and coprimality choices are also only sketched and do not repair that missing invariant.

judgment.reason: Its Eisenstein-factorization lemma is not proved. Choosing split prime factors does not show that their product is associated to an element of the special form u-omega; this is the essential unestablished claim.

The auxiliary fact is merely asserted through an unjustified Eisenstein-integer selection argument. It does not demonstrate the existence of y-omega with the required prescribed pairwise-coprime norm factors.

The stated factorization lemma is not a standard consequence in the form claimed: selecting split primes and nonassociate factors does not establish that their product can be arranged as z-omega. The core construction is missing.
The asserted standard lemma is unsupported. In particular, the claimed construction of x-omega with arbitrarily many suitable conjugation-stable factors is neither explained nor shown possible.
